questions.code: for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i += 3) cout << i << " ";
questions.e: i takes 1, 4, 7, 10. The next value, 13, fails i <= 10, so the loop stops.
Nested loops multiply: the inner loop runs 4 times for each of the 3 outer rounds, so 3 × 4 = 12.

questions.q: In FizzBuzz, which check has to come first?
questions.e: 15 is divisible by 3 too. If “divisible by 3” comes first, 15 prints Fizz and the FizzBuzz case is never reached. The most specific case goes first.
break leaves the loop as soon as i reaches 3, before i++ runs again.
continue skips the even numbers, so only 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 is added.

questions.q: Which correctly checks that x is between 10 and 20 (inclusive)?
questions.e: Both sides must be written and joined with &&. 10 <= x <= 20 compiles but compares (10 <= x), which is 0 or 1, with 20.
Each round removes one digit (4071 → 407 → 40 → 4 → 0), so the loop counts the 4 digits.
